messages.subject: Generating an estimate of expected flock size
parts:
Dear Tim, Jeff, and list,

Tim-

I also had similar discrepancies in variance estimates when computed analyt=
ically vs. the bootstrap. For example on a survey with flock size ranging =
from 1 - 25,000 variance estimates were 25% and 46% for the analytical and =
bootstrap estimates respectively.

Jeff- I had essentially the same question as Tim in regards to implementin=
g the ln(flocksize) as a covariate so any info you might have on that would=
be much appreciated. Also, I am guessing you saw Steve Buckland's respons=
e suggesting treating the groups as individuals, and I am just curious as t=
o whether you would be more inclined to try the ln(flocksize approach) or t=
he individuals approach given our situation.

Thanks to everyone for their input and help,
Brendan Shirkey shirk...@osu.edu

messages.subject: Re: Generating an estimate of expected flock size
parts:
Brendan Shirkey wrote:
> > Dear Tim, Jeff, and list,
> >
> > Tim-
> >

> > I also had similar discrepancies in variance estimates when computed analytically vs. the bootstrap. For example on a survey with flock size ranging from 1 - 25,000 variance estimates were 25% and 46% for the analytical and bootstrap estimates respectively.
> >
Are these %cvs presumably? With this distribution of group sizes with a
long tail (ie a few with a large group size), I expect this could happen
but I don't have any advice as to which would be better.
> > Jeff- I had essentially the same question as Tim in regards to implementing the ln(flocksize) as a covariate so any info you might have on that would be much appreciated.
The abundance estimate would be constructed in the same way as s_i/p_i
where s_i is group size and p_i is probability of detecting group i
which would use ln(s_i) as a scale covariate. For example with
half-normal p_i(x)=exp(-(x/(sigma_i)^2/2) and ln(sigma_i)=B_0+B_1*ln(s_i).
> > Also, I am guessing you saw Steve Buckland's response suggesting treating the groups as individuals, and I am just curious as to whether you would be more inclined to try the ln(flocksize approach) or the individuals approach given our situation.
> >
> >
Steve's idea is fine as long as you collected the data in a way that you
could implement that and you then used a bootstrap variance to handle
dependence in sightings. I agree that assessing center of a large group
could be problematic to get its distance especially if you flew directly
over the group.

--jeff
